plain_english: The boundless manifold of difference, treated in brief and in full, is set forth; and now, in due order, comes the reckoning of its divisions from water onward, from root to end.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃkṣepavistarakṛtaṃ bhedānantyaṃ pratāyate /
punar jalādimūlāntabhedasaṃkalanakramāt // [AgMsv_1.965]

plain_english: Great is the upsurge of manifold variety born of difference and its subdivisions. Thus from earth to the end of the pradhāna-principle the course has been taught fifteenfold, and the sakala, whose nature spans from puruṣa to kalā, is neither knower nor means of knowledge.
sanskrit_cite:
bhūyān bhedaprabhedottho vaicitryavisarodayaḥ

evaṃ dharātaḥ prabhṛti pradhānatattvāntam uktaṃ daśapañcadhaiva /
puṃsaḥ kalāntaṃ sakalaḥ svarūpabhūto na mātā na ca mānarūpaḥ // [AgMsv_1.966]

plain_english: The thirteenfold nature is therefore established here: in the night-state the layākala keeps his own nature, in the middle the vijñānākala-nature, and in the domain of vidyā the mantra-become-nature.
sanskrit_cite:
trayodaśātmatvam ato 'tra niṣṭhitaṃ niśi svarūpaṃ tu bhavel layākalaḥ /
madhye tu vijñānakalasvarūpatā vidyāpade mantragatasvarūpatā // [AgMsv_1.967]

plain_english: In the Īśa domain abides the class of Mantreśas; now, in the most auspicious abode, devotion to that Lord — and each prior stage therein reveals its own order of knower and measure — so that, with no other knower, the self-luminous state of Śiva flashes forth ever one; yet from the Mantreśa-Īśas issue divisions numbered three, five, seven, nine, and three.
sanskrit_cite:
aiśe mantreśavargasthitir atha suśive dhāmni tannāthaniṣṭhā pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ ca tatra prakaṭayati nijāṃ mātṛmānavyavasthām /
tenānanyapramātṛ sphurati śivapadaṃ svaprakāśaṃ sadaikaṃ mantreśeśānatas tu triśaramuninavatryakṣasaṃkhyāvibhedāḥ // [AgMsv_1.968]

plain_english: And śakti, for our part, is undivided from the power-holder; thereby this separateness does not indeed amount to difference. Where knowerhood is absent, moreover, no śakti exists — so such a nature is not endowed with power.
sanskrit_cite:
śaktiś ca no śaktimato vibhinnā tenaiti no bhedam iyaṃ pṛthaktvam /
amātṛtāyāṃ na ca śaktir asti tena svarūpaṃ na hi śaktiyuktam // [AgMsv_1.969]

plain_english: Whatever light shines here without difference from the earth-principle — that itself is Lord Śiva: earth is brahman, the supreme.
sanskrit_cite:
dharātattvāvibhedena yaḥ prakāśaḥ prakāśate /
sa eva śivanātho 'tra pṛthivī brahma tatparam // [AgMsv_1.970]

plain_english: Those who, from Śivas will, impel the ones intent on bestowing the powers abiding in the earth-principle — they are the Mantramaheśvaras.
sanskrit_cite:
dharātattvagatāḥ siddhīr vitarītuṃ samudyatān /
prerayanti śivecchāto ye te mantramaheśvarāḥ // [AgMsv_1.971]

plain_english: The Mantreśas, being impelled, and the mantras clearly declaring it, having cultivated through the Śiva-science the yoga that abides in the earth-principle.
sanskrit_cite:
preryamāṇās tu mantreśā mantrās tadvācakāḥ sphuṭam /
dharātattvagataṃ yogam abhyasya śivavidyayā // [AgMsv_1.972]

plain_english: But not like the dualists — Pāśava, Sāṃkhya, Vaiṣṇava and the rest — who, never attaining the firm abode, possess but vijñānākala-nature.
sanskrit_cite:
na tu pāśavasāṃkhyīyavaiṣṇavādidvitādṛśā /
aprāptadhruvadhāmāno vijñānakalatājuṣaḥ // [AgMsv_1.973]

plain_english: Those who, through enjoyment of just such principles, reached dissolution at the kalpas end — abiding as in deep sleep, they are here the pralayakevalas.
sanskrit_cite:
tāvattattvopabhogena ye kalpānte layaṃ gatāḥ /
sauṣuptāvasthitau yadvat te 'tra pralayakevalāḥ // [AgMsv_1.974]

plain_english: In deep sleep the dissolvedness in the principles is indeed plainly seen — for otherwise, whence this fixed conjunction with dreaming, just so?
sanskrit_cite:
sauṣupte tattvalīnatvaṃ sphuṭam eva hi lakṣyate /
anyathā niyatasvapnasaṃsṛṣṭir iyatī kutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.975]

plain_english: Deep sleep too shines forth varied — pure and impure and the rest — since variety is seen in such memories as I-did-not-sleep and happily.
sanskrit_cite:
sauṣuptam api citraṃ ca svacchāsvacchādi bhāsate /
asvāpsaṃ sukham ityādismṛtivaicitryadarśanāt // [AgMsv_1.976]

plain_english: Here the persons, whose massed malas mix with the upsurge of māyā and karma, climbing upon earth, are to be known as sakalas.
sanskrit_cite:
māyākarmasamullāsasaṃmiśritamalābilāḥ /
dharādhirohiṇo jñeyāḥ sakalā iha pudgalāḥ // [AgMsv_1.977]

plain_english: Whatever agitation there is in settling each ones own task within just this sevenfold order — that indeed is called the seven of the śaktis; and thence.
sanskrit_cite:
asyaiva saptakasya svasvavyāpāraprakalpane /
prakṣobho yas tad evoktaṃ śaktīnāṃ saptakaṃ tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.978]

plain_english: Śiva is of unfallen consciousness-nature; but his three śaktis — they have, by force of autonomy, assumed the form of subject and object.
sanskrit_cite:
śivo 'vicyutacidrūpas tisras tacchaktayas tu yāḥ /
tāḥ svātantryavaśopāttagrahītṛgrāhyarūpikāḥ // [AgMsv_1.979]

plain_english: By excess of the subject-share, by upsurge of the object-share — seven and seven — yet one thing, merely inert, human-natured.
sanskrit_cite:
grahītṛbhāgodrekeṇa grāhyabhāgocchalatvataḥ /
sapta sapteti yat tv ekaṃ jaḍamātraṃ narātmakam // [AgMsv_1.980]

plain_english: Its nature is therefore settled threefold, per tattva; and in the ungraspable object — what? — the sixteen tuṭis are moments.
sanskrit_cite:
tatsvarūpaṃ tatas traidhaṃ pratitattvaṃ vyavasthitam /
kiṃ cārthe khalu nirgrāhye tuṭayaḥ ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇāḥ // [AgMsv_1.981]

plain_english: They are severally reckoned from the two-and-a-quarter-finger entrance; and therein the first is of the very taste of partless supreme nondualism.
sanskrit_cite:
sapādadvyaṅgulāveśāt pratyekaṃ parikalpitāḥ /
tatrādyaḥ paramādvaitanirvibhāgarasātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.982]

plain_english: The last, though, is not distinctly conceived apart from identity with object-nature; the penultimate is fully conceived as the grasper of its nature.
sanskrit_cite:
antyas tu grāhyatādātmyān na pṛthak pravibhāvyate /
upāntyas tatsvarūpasya grāhakaḥ paribhāvvyate // [AgMsv_1.983]

plain_english: And the first seven there has gone to imagelessness — skilled in covering the shade of the sequentially unfolding portions of imagining.
sanskrit_cite:
ādyaṃ ca saptakaṃ tatra nirvikalpakatāṃ gatam /
kramonmiṣadvikalpāṃśacchāyācchādanakovidam // [AgMsv_1.984]

plain_english: For the wise know that very nature as Śiva consisting of supreme śakti; the second seven therein consists of the parāpara plane.
sanskrit_cite:
tad eva śivarūpaṃ hi paraśaktyātmakaṃ viduḥ /
dvitīyaṃ saptakaṃ tatra parāparapadātmakam // [AgMsv_1.985]

plain_english: Sung as vikalpa — thus difference is made to appear; for that, in this subtle consciousness, they are intent on impelling.
sanskrit_cite:
vikalpa iti saṃgītam iti bhedo 'vabhāsyate /
tad asyāṃ sūkṣmasaṃvittau kalanāya samudyatāḥ // [AgMsv_1.986]

plain_english: Whatever form they experience — what is there in boastings about it? But what is held: even the tuṭis, in the lessening of difference that comes from sequence.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃvedayante yadrūpaṃ tatra kiṃ vā vikatthanaiḥ /
kramāt tu bhedanyūnatve tuṭīnām api yo mataḥ // [AgMsv_1.987]

plain_english: The diminution of conceptualization is characterized by the absence of conceptualization, just as one afflicted by long suffering later attains a state of happiness.
sanskrit_cite:
vikalpasya ca nirhrāso nirvikalpopalakṣaṇam /
yathā hi ciraduḥkhārtaḥ paścād āttasukhasthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.988]

plain_english: Just as someone who has found happiness forgets earlier suffering by resting in that happiness, so people who are firmly established in awareness, even when conceptual thought has gone, no longer cling to it.
sanskrit_cite:
vismaraty eva tadduḥkhaṃ sukhaviśrāntivartmanā /
tathā gatavikalpe 'pi rūḍhāḥ saṃvedane janāḥ // [AgMsv_1.989]

plain_english: People who rely on conceptual thinking do not lay claim to that deeper state; but when conceptualization dissolves, awareness becomes free of thought and ultimately true, and its own nature shines forth. In this way, clear understanding arises for those who attend to it with effort.
sanskrit_cite:
vikalpaviśrāntibalāt tāṃ vṛttiṃ nābhimanvate /

vikalpanirhrāsavaśena yāti vikalpavandhyā paramārthasatyā /
saṃvitsvarūpaprakaṭatvam itthaṃ tatrāvadhāne yatatāṃ subuddhiḥ // [AgMsv_1.990]

plain_english: This attentiveness is said to occur in the relation between the grasped, the grasper, and their awareness, because in that context it is connected with the attainment of the desired result.
sanskrit_cite:
grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittau saṃbandhe sāvadhānatā /
iyaṃ sā bhaṇyate tatra yatheṣṭaphalayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.991]

plain_english: For this very reason, because of the abundance of its divisions, the worlds too become variegated; and no transgression of this explanation is accepted.
sanskrit_cite:
ata eva hi tadbhedabāhulyād bhuvanāny api /
vicitratvaṃ prayāntīti na cātikrama iṣyate // [AgMsv_1.992]

plain_english: This reality appears both with sequence and without sequence; but since time has already been refuted, and since the ultimate reality of space cannot be established by reasoning, neither can be taken as ultimately real.
sanskrit_cite:
sakramākramam evedaṃ kālasya prākpradūsaṇāt /
diśaś ca paramārthatvaṃ naiva yuktyopapadyate // [AgMsv_1.993]

plain_english: For no single thing produces the cognition of before and after, and difference based on limiting conditions is not itself a real entity; so how could that cognition be postulated as ultimately grounded?
sanskrit_cite:
pūrvāparapratītiṃ hi naikā sā kurute tathā /
upādhibhedo no vastu tat kathaṃ sā prakalpyatām // [AgMsv_1.994]

plain_english: The supreme Lord, who fashions the sphere of space and time out of his own bliss, declared the basis on which one thing is said to be superior to another by its qualities.
sanskrit_cite:
yo hi yasmādguṇotkṛṣṭa ity ataḥ parameśvaraḥ /
abhāṣata nijānandakḷptadikkālamaṇḍalaḥ // [AgMsv_1.995]

plain_english: Thus, for those who wish to enter into this variegated nature of reality, a threefold division of absorptions has been described, because the means differ.
sanskrit_cite:
tad evaṃ tattvarūpe 'smin vicitre pravivikṣatām /
upāyabhedāt traividhyaṃ samāveśeṣu varṇitam // [AgMsv_1.996]

plain_english: The Śāmbhava means is without method; next comes the means based on consciousness; and the Āṇava means, based on the inert, is also regarded as taking many forms.
sanskrit_cite:
anupāyaḥ śāṃbhavo 'sau cidupāyas tataḥ param /
jaḍopāyas tv āṇavaḥ syāt sa cāpi bahudhā mataḥ // [AgMsv_1.997]

plain_english: Even within what is non-inert, an appearance of inertness arises through the power of the supreme Lord, as in the channels, senses, and external supports; therefore these can still function as a means grounded in consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
ajaḍe 'pi jaḍābhāsaḥ pārameśvaryayogataḥ /
nāḍīkaraṇabāhyādes tena saṃvidupāyatā // [AgMsv_1.998]

plain_english: When experience rests on the functioning of the senses and there is a grasping of external forms, that clear and repeatedly continuous condition is the waking state.
sanskrit_cite:
tatrākṣavṛttim āśritya bāhyākāragraho hi yaḥ /
tajjāgratsphuṭam āsīnam anubandhi punaḥ punaḥ // [AgMsv_1.999]

plain_english: Dream is a construction made by one's own imagination and is the reverse of waking; and the experience belonging to the layākala arises under the force of karma tending toward dissolution, but not in a stable way.
sanskrit_cite:
ātmasaṃkalpanirmāṇaṃ svapno jāgradviparyayaḥ /
layākalasya yo bhogaḥ layakarmavaśān na tu // [AgMsv_1.1000]

plain_english: That experience would not be stable, because there is no night-like obscuration; deep sleep is the non-awareness of pleasure and so on. For the jñānākala, due to mere impurity, there is only bare experience.
sanskrit_cite:
sthiro bhaven niśābhāvāt suptaṃ saukhyādyavedane /
jñānākalasya malataḥ kevalād bhogamātrataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1001]

plain_english: Inert and non-inert things appear as inherently distinct and differentiated; yet in the fourth state there abide the three groups: the mantra beings, their lords, and the overlords.
sanskrit_cite:
bhedavantaḥ svato bhinnāś cikīrṣyante jaḍājaḍāḥ /
turye tatra sthitā mantratannāthādhīśvarās trayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1002]

plain_english: To the extent that entities become capable of receiving a share of Bhairava-awareness, their own separate essence melts away and they become non-different by themselves.
sanskrit_cite:
yāvad bhairavabodhāṃśapraveśanasahiṣṇavaḥ /
bhāvā vigaladātmīyasārāḥ svayam abhedinaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1003]

plain_english: They would abide in the state beyond the fourth. In this fifteenfold scheme, whatever form appears clear and distinct should be regarded as the waking state.
sanskrit_cite:
turyātītapade saṃsyur iti pañcadaśātmake /
yasya yad yad sphuṭaṃ rūpaṃ taj jāgrad iti manyatām // [AgMsv_1.1004]

plain_english: That same form, when it appears unstable, is dream of that kind; but when it appears unclear, that is deep sleep, including what appears before it.
sanskrit_cite:
tad evāsthiram ābhāti svarūpaṃ svapna īdṛśaḥ /
asphuṭaṃ tu yad ābhāti suptaṃ tat tat puro 'pi yat // [AgMsv_1.1005]

plain_english: The continuity by which the three states arise and are held together, like the thread in a garland, should be understood as the fourth state present through all differences.
sanskrit_cite:
tritayasyānusaṃdhis tu yadvaśād upajāyate /
sraksūtratulyaṃ tatturyaṃ sarvabhedeṣu gṛhyatām // [AgMsv_1.1006]

plain_english: But that which shines with the fullness of nonduality and melts away all distinctions is declared to be the state beyond the fourth; one should apply this understanding everywhere.
sanskrit_cite:
yat tv advaitabharollāsi drāvitāśeṣabhedakam /
turyātītaṃ tu tat prāhur itthaṃ sarvatra yojayet // [AgMsv_1.1007]

plain_english: For the layākala, its own form is waking, and the prior states are counted as dream and so on; the wise person should trace this whole sequence in every case.
sanskrit_cite:
layākale hi svaṃ rūpaṃ jāgrattatpūrvavṛtti tu /
svapnādīti kramaṃ sarvaṃ sarvatrānusared budhaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1008]

plain_english: Even within the one full Lord, consciousness is said to be the state beyond the fourth, bliss is the fourth, and will itself is the seed-ground corresponding to deep sleep.
sanskrit_cite:
ekatrāpi prabhau pūrṇe citturyātītam ucyate /
ānandas turyam icchaiva bījabhūmiḥ suṣuptatā // [AgMsv_1.1009]

plain_english: Knowledge corresponds to the dream state, and action is remembered as the waking state; in this same context arise the yogic designations beginning with piṇḍastha.
sanskrit_cite:
jñānaṃ tu svapnavṛttitvaṃ kriyā jāgrad iti smṛtā /
atraiva yogabhūmyutthāḥ saṃjñāḥ piṇḍasthatādayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1010]

plain_english: Classifications such as sarvatobhadra are constructed by those who rely on discriminative analysis; because the fourfold structure is present in each case, further elaborations arise in the expanded scheme.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvatobhadratādyās tu prasaṃkhyājñāninirmitāḥ /
ekaikatra catūrūpasadbhāvād vitate tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1011]

plain_english: In one place there is fourfoldness, then threefoldness, then oneness; yet the one Lord Bhairava remains, with all universal forms flashing forth within him.
sanskrit_cite:
catūrūpatvam ekatra tritvaṃ paścād athaikatā /
ekas tu bhairavo nāthaḥ prollasadviśvarūpakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1012]

plain_english: The one reality, present in every state from Śiva to the limited individual, is this entire path itself, abiding in non-difference from Bhairava.
sanskrit_cite:
ekaḥ śivādisakalaparyantasthitisaṃgataḥ /
so 'yaṃ samasta evādhvā bhairavābhedavṛttimān // [AgMsv_1.1013]

plain_english: By its own freedom, that same reality shines forth as autonomous; when it abides in the form of the knowing subject, it is recognized as the path of mantras.
sanskrit_cite:
tatsvātantryāt svatantratvam aśnuvāno 'vabhāsate /
so 'yaṃ mātṛsvarūpastho mantrādhveti vibhāvyate // [AgMsv_1.1014]

plain_english: In the form of valid cognition, this reality is called the path of phonemes; when it takes the form of the means of knowledge, it becomes the path of words.
sanskrit_cite:
pramārūpatayā so 'yaṃ varṇādhveti nirucyate /
pramāṇarūpatām etya prayāty eṣa padādhvatām // [AgMsv_1.1015]

plain_english: Without abandoning its role as the means of knowledge, it moves toward objecthood through conceptualization; joined with the knower, it becomes the path of limited powers.
sanskrit_cite:
pramāṇarūpatāveśam aparityajya meyatām /
gacchan saṃkalpanayogāt kalādhvā mātṛsaṃgataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1016]

plain_english: When it is purely connected with objecthood, it should be understood as the path of principles; when it serves as the support of that grossness, it is described as the path of worlds.
sanskrit_cite:
śuddhe prameyatāyoge sa tattvādhveti gṛhyatām /
tatsthaulyādhāratāyogād bhuvanādhveti varṇitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1017]

plain_english: For when the state of what can be expressed is swallowed by the reflective awareness of consciousness, it becomes intent on cognition and protection grounded in Śiva's knowledge and action.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi cidvimarśena grastā vācyadaśā yadā /
śivajñānakriyāyattamananatrāṇatatparā // [AgMsv_1.1018]

plain_english: From its skill in the eager play of all its powers, the mantra path, whose nature is Śiva, first arises swiftly and with force.
sanskrit_cite:
aśeṣaśaktipaṭalīlīlālāmpaṭyapāṭavāt /
mantrādhvā rabhasena drāk prāg udbhūtaḥ śivātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1019]

plain_english: For the one who relishes repose in surging consciousness alone, the powers are unrestricted because of the capacity to name everything.
sanskrit_cite:
ucchalatsaṃvidāmātraviśrāntyāsvādayoginaḥ /
sarvābhidhānasāmarthyād aniyantritaśaktayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1020]

plain_english: The powers are emanated with operations ranging from meanings that arise with the self down to the earth, encompassing all those objects within the play of consciousness in their own self.
sanskrit_cite:
sṛṣṭāḥ svātmasahotthārthadharāparyantavṛttayaḥ /
svātmīye cidvilasite tāvato 'rthān nijātmani // [AgMsv_1.1021]

plain_english: Infants and even animal knowers, who have no share in linguistic convention, still apprehend things and bear a real consciousness in the form of valid cognition.
sanskrit_cite:
āmṛśantaḥ pramārūpāṃ satyāṃ bibhrati saṃvidam /
bālās tiryakpramātāro ye 'py asaṃketabhāginaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1022]

plain_english: Even they, relying on this own consciousness of theirs—whose essence is an uncontrived impression and which is both differentiated and undifferentiated—attain a varied state of being knowers.
sanskrit_cite:
te 'py akṛtrimasaṃskārasārām enāṃ svasaṃvidam /
bhinnabhinnām upāśritya yānti citrāṃ pramātṛtām // [AgMsv_1.1023]

plain_english: If linguistic conventions become firmly established in this uncontrived consciousness of infinite phonemes, then even they come to operate in a non-conventional way.
sanskrit_cite:
asyām akṛtrimānantavarṇasaṃvidi rūḍhatām /
saṃketā yānti cet te 'pi yānty asaṃketavṛttitām // [AgMsv_1.1024]

plain_english: But without this innate consciousness, all the many conventions that are made could never find rest in the mind, because they would depend on yet other conventions.
sanskrit_cite:
anayā tu vinā sarve saṃketā bahuśaḥ kṛtāḥ /
naiva cetasi viśrāntiṃ saṃketāntarayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1025]

plain_english: They would never find rest, because of infinite regress and because that would destroy the very root; so how, indeed, could a child even be instructed in a convention?
sanskrit_cite:
vrajeyur anavasthānān mūlakṣatikaratvataḥ /
tatrāpi khalu saṃkete bālo vyutpādyatāṃ kutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1026]

plain_english: Therefore, this infinite, non-māyic collection of phonemes, accompanied by the reflective awareness of consciousness, is always unfolding.
sanskrit_cite:
tenānantas tv amāyīyo yo varṇagrāma īdṛśaḥ /
sa cidvimarśasacivaḥ sadaiva pravijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.1027]

plain_english: And from that very source the māyic phonemes came into being; it is understood that those non-māyic phonemes are indeed their power.
sanskrit_cite:
tata eva ca māyīyā varṇāḥ sūtiṃ vitenire /
teṣāṃ te khalv amāyīyā vīryam ity avadhāryate // [AgMsv_1.1028]

plain_english: For when others' utterances are heard, if one's own cognition remains veiled, that dull person does not become a knowing subject with respect to that meaning.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi paravākyeṣu śruteṣv āvṛṇute nijā /
pramā yasya jaḍo nāsau tatrārthe yāti mātṛtām // [AgMsv_1.1029]

plain_english: But if one's own cognition, bearing differentiation within it, enters into awareness within one's own mass of māyic phonemes, that person attains the state of being a knower.
sanskrit_cite:
yasya tu svapramā bodhe praviśed bhedagarbhagā /
māyīyavarṇapuñje sve sa pramātṛtvam ṛcchati // [AgMsv_1.1030]

plain_english: To the extent that the uncreated, innate form predominates, to that same extent a gradation of aesthetic wonder is produced.
sanskrit_cite:
yathā yathā cākṛtakaṃ tadrūpam atiricyate /
tathā tathā camatkāratāratamyaṃ prakalpyate // [AgMsv_1.1031]

plain_english: But when that surge becomes great, those established in the nature of intuitive insight certainly attain, in every way, excellence in poetry and eloquence.
sanskrit_cite:
tadudrekamahattve tu pratibhātmani niṣṭhitāḥ /
dhruvaṃ kavitvavaktṛtvaśālitāṃ yānti sarvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1032]

plain_english: Therefore, in the perfection of speech, the phonemes are contemplated; for that very reason they are kept secret and spoken only by one who maintains secrecy.
sanskrit_cite:
ata eva hi vāksiddhau varṇānāṃ samupāsyatā /
teṣām eva tatas tena guptā guptena bhāṣitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1033]

plain_english: Then, insofar as there is the Lord's constant repose, it projects many phonemes at once, well established in fulfilling the portions of experience.
sanskrit_cite:
tato yāvadvibhoḥ śaśvadviśrāntir yugapadbahūn /
varṇān udṛṅkya bhogāṃśaparipūraṇasusthitān // [AgMsv_1.1034]

plain_english: To that extent, this path of words, resting on the level of the object, becomes the first sprout within the mass of conventions bound up with worldly existence.
sanskrit_cite:
tāvad eva padādhvāsau meyabhūmim upāśritaḥ /
saṃsāramṛtasaṃketasaṃghāte prathamāṅkuraḥ // [AgMsv_1.1035]

plain_english: Thus it is ascertained that objecthood, the state of being the knower, and the state of being the means of knowledge all belong to the thirty-sixfold collection of principles.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ prameyatā mātṛbhāvo mānatvam apy atha /
ṣaṭtriṃśadātmanas tattvakalāpasyeti niścitam // [AgMsv_1.1036]

plain_english: There, all this shines forth in the unchanging supreme Lord in the form of a reflection, and not as something external.
sanskrit_cite:
tatra sarvaṃ vibhāty etat parameśitari dhruve /
pratibimbasvarūpeṇa na tu bāhyatayā yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1037]

plain_english: In the sky of consciousness, in Śiva alone, such divided cognitions of various bodies appear to worldly beings, just as a snake and the like appear in a rope.
sanskrit_cite:
cidvyomny eva śive tattaddehādimatir īdṛśī /
bhinnā saṃsāriṇāṃ bhāti rajjau sarpādikā yathā // [AgMsv_1.1038]

plain_english: Because the settled view before the body's death belongs to the realm of dream, what kind of other body or bodily arising after death could there really be?
sanskrit_cite:
yataḥ prāgdehamaraṇasiddhāntaḥ svapnagocaraḥ /
dehāntarādir maraṇāt kīdṛg vā dehasaṃbhavaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1039]

plain_english: In a dream, particular details appear by the force of the unfolding of mere appearance, but they are not produced as independent realities in that way.
sanskrit_cite:
svapne tu pratibhāmātrasāmānyaprathanād balāt /
viśeṣāḥ pratibhāsante na bhāvyante 'pi te tathā // [AgMsv_1.1040]

plain_english: Just as some śālagrāma stones contain varied forms within them, so the inner delineations of the levels from māyā downward belong to the variegated heart of consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
sāligrāmopalāḥ kecic citrākṛtihṛdo yathā /
tathā māyādibhūmyantalekhāś citrahṛdayaś citaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1041]

plain_english: Cities, oceans, mountains, and the like follow that will; they are not by themselves entities that independently function as existent or nonexistent causes and effects.
sanskrit_cite:
nagarārṇavaśailādyās tadicchānuvidhāyinaḥ /
na svayaṃ sadasadrūpakāraṇākaraṇātmakāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1042]

plain_english: Whether by cutting off or setting in motion a long-established rule, or even where no rule has yet taken root, this Bhairava of the sky of consciousness remains independent.
sanskrit_cite:
ciraprarūḍhe niyame samucchedāt pravartanāt /
arūḍhe 'pi svatantro 'yaṃ sthitaś cidvyomabhairavaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1043]

plain_english: In that state which shares nondifference with Bhairava, full of one consciousness alone, the absence of the recognition 'I am thus' is what differentiates the realm of beings.
sanskrit_cite:
ekacinmātrasaṃpūrṇabhairavābhedabhāgini /
evam asmīty anāmarśo bhedako bhāvamaṇḍale // [AgMsv_1.1044]

plain_english: Just as no other agent is established in a dream by any means of knowledge, so too the creation should be understood as belonging to one's own independent awareness.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvapramāṇair no siddhaṃ svapne kartrantaraṃ yathā /
svasaṃvidaḥ svatantrāyās tathā sargo 'pi budhyatām // [AgMsv_1.1045]

plain_english: One who plays in the mind's variegated city and garden knows: 'I alone abide as all these beings that have come to be, and they are nothing but consciousness.'
sanskrit_cite:
cittacitrapurodyāne krīḍann evaṃ hi vetti yaḥ /
aham eva sthito bhāvair bhūtaiś cinmātrakair iti // [AgMsv_1.1046]

plain_english: The varied experiences of 'I am born' and 'I am dead' appear in the unborn and deathless, on the wall of the mind, as projections of one's own imagination.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ jāto mṛto 'smīti janmamṛtyuvicitratāḥ /
ajanmany amṛtau bhānti cittabhittau svakalpināḥ // [AgMsv_1.1047]

plain_english: Being this world or another world is only a matter of awareness; even amid apparent divisions of time, part, awareness, and place, it remains undivided.
sanskrit_cite:
parehasaṃvidāmātraṃ paralokehalokatā /
kiṃtv akālakalāsaṃviddeśabhede 'py abhedinī // [AgMsv_1.1048]

plain_english: If this creation were merely material and not made of consciousness, then no one could perceive even a single mountain from within it.
sanskrit_cite:
abhaviṣyad ayaṃ sargo mūrtaś cen na tu cinmayaḥ /
tad avekṣyata tanmadhyāt kenaiko 'pi dharādharaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1049]

plain_english: When one examines the elements, subtle elements, and the rest in terms of support and what is supported, in the end it is the consciousness-power, identical with Śiva's own nature, that upholds them.
sanskrit_cite:
bhūtatanmātravargāder ādhārādheyacarcane /
ante saṃvinmayī śaktiḥ śivarūpaiva dhāriṇī // [AgMsv_1.1050]

plain_english: Therefore cognition itself is the agent; that manifestation is Śiva in his own self. For that reason, this power is called the common ground.
sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt pratītir evetthaṃ kartrī sā pratibhā śivaḥ /
atra svātmani te tena śaktiḥ sādhārasaṃjñitā // [AgMsv_1.1051]

plain_english: Even what is imagined and seems without support does not fall away, because the universe rests in its own supporting power; reflect on it in this way.
sanskrit_cite:
sāṃkalpikaṃ nirādhāram api naiva pataty adhaḥ /
svādhāraśaktau viśrānter viśvam itthaṃ vimṛśyatām // [AgMsv_1.1052]

plain_english: From the fixation of the dense 'I' and so on arises the state beginning with earth, until at last the recognition 'I am consciousness' is fulfilled as the identity of Bhairava.
sanskrit_cite:
asyā ghanāham ityādirūḍher eva dharāditā /
yāvad ante cidasmīti nirvṛttā bhairavātmatā // [AgMsv_1.1053]

plain_english: Like blue and other colors in a jewel or in a rainbow's light, so appearances are in Śiva; but in ultimate truth they have no real arising or passing away.
sanskrit_cite:
maṇāv indrāyudhe bhāsa iva nīlādayaḥ śive /
paramārthata eṣāṃ tu nodayavyayayogitā // [AgMsv_1.1054]

plain_english: To say that creation happens in space or in time is incoherent, for the creation of the conscious Lord includes space and time as well.
sanskrit_cite:
deśe kāle 'tra vā sṛṣṭir ity etad asamañjasam /
cidātmano hi devasya sṛṣṭir dikkālayor api // [AgMsv_1.1055]

plain_english: Within what is taken as waking, in a span of three and a half cubits and a single watch of time, separate dreams arise with their own varied measures of space and time.
sanskrit_cite:
jāgarābhimate sārdhahastatritayagocare /
prahare ca pṛthaksvapnāś citradikkālamāninaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1056]

plain_english: Therefore we do not regard a moment as anything fixed, for even within a single moment of action there are many swift actions.
sanskrit_cite:
ata eva kṣaṇaṃ nāma na kiṃcid api manmahe /
kriyākṣaṇe 'pi hy ekasmin bahvyaḥ santi drutāḥ kriyāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1057]

plain_english: Therefore those who hold that the contraction of beings ends in a moment surely rely, through this narrow channel, on a view grounded in emptiness.
sanskrit_cite:
tena ye bhāvasaṃkocaṃ kṣaṇāntaṃ pratipedire /
te nūnam anayā nālyā śūnyadṛṣṭyavalambinaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1058]

plain_english: Therefore the one who, by his independence, is able to make existent beings appear empty and likewise make the nonexistent appear clearly is the supreme Lord.
sanskrit_cite:
tad ya eva sato bhāvāñ śūnyīkatuṃ tahtāsataḥ /
sphuṭīkartuṃ svatantratvād īśaḥ sa parameśvaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.1059]

plain_english: Thus the supreme Lord is proclaimed as having the universe as his form; no separate entity such as earth or the rest can be established as independently real in that way.
sanskrit_cite:
tad itthaṃ parameśāno viśvarūpaḥ pragīyate /
na tu bhinnasya kasyāpi dharāder upapannatā // [AgMsv_1.1060]

plain_english: This has already been said before, so it is not examined again in detail; many refutations of external objects have already been composed.
sanskrit_cite:
uktaṃ caitat puraiveti na bhūyaḥ pravivicyate /
bahubhiś cāpi bāhyārthadūṣaṇā pravyaracyata // [AgMsv_1.1061]

plain_english: But if things are so, how can karma be connected with its fruit in birth and death? Has the previously stated freedom of consciousness been completely forgotten?
sanskrit_cite:
nanv itthaṃ janmamaraṇe karmaṇaḥ phalayogitā /
kathaṃ syāt kin nu pūrvoktaṃ citsvātantryaṃ suvisṛmtam // [AgMsv_1.1062]

plain_english: For this free consciousness makes things shine forth just as it wills, and so they truly appear; it contains all forms within itself, and this is firmly established.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi citsvatantreyaṃ yathā bhāsayate tathā /
satyaṃ bhāty akhilākāragarbhā sā ceti niścitam // [AgMsv_1.1063]

plain_english: Just as sweetness is present in every atom of sugarcane in every way, so in each ultimate atom there abides a state consisting of the whole creation.
sanskrit_cite:
ikṣau pratyaṇu mādhuryaṃ yathā sarvātmanā tathā /
pratyekaparamāṇau hi sarvasṛṣṭimayī sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.1064]

plain_english: But those learned people who do not know the root principle and dispute this are surely engaged only in protecting their own fantasy-kingdom.
sanskrit_cite:
ajñātatattvamūlās tu vivadante 'tra ye budhāḥ /
nūnaṃ nijamanorājyarakṣāyai te samudyatāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1065]

plain_english: The idea that this is located in breath, in space, in consciousness, in the external world, or anywhere at all is a delusion, arising from ignorance and swollen by the seeming absence of freedom produced by restriction.
sanskrit_cite:
prāṇe khe citi bāhye vā kutrāpīdam iti bhramaḥ /
ajñatvāt tanniyatyutthasvātantryābhāvajṛmbhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1066]

plain_english: Therefore, the awareness of one's own consciousness appears here as birth; but beforehand consciousness does not appear in a form suited to its freedom.
sanskrit_cite:
ataḥ svasaṃvidāmarśo janmatveneha bhāsate /
purastāt tu na saṃvittiḥ svātantryocitarūpiṇī // [AgMsv_1.1067]

plain_english: Here the former consciousness is called previous karma; therefore, a consciousness that obstructs that former consciousness brings about the destruction of karma.
sanskrit_cite:
prāktanī saṃvid eveha pūrvakarmeti bhāṣyate /
tatsaṃvidbādhikā saṃvitkarmakṣayakarī tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1068]

plain_english: Just as in a dream something not actually done can flash forth as 'done by me' and be seen to give fruit, the same is true of karma in the waking state.
sanskrit_cite:
akṛtaṃ ca yathā svapne mayā kṛtam iti sphuret /
phaladā dṛśyate saiva vārtā jāgrati karmaṇaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1069]

plain_english: And so, if even a single higher consciousness arises in someone, consisting in the burning up of the fruit of the mass of past karma, that person does not undergo that fruit.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā ca prācyakarmaughaphalasaṃploṣaṇātmikā /
yasyaikāpy uttarodeti saṃvit sa phalabhāṅ na hi // [AgMsv_1.1070]

plain_english: Moreover, through the clear flashing forth of many consciousnesses, even disrepute can become repute, bearing abundant fruit like a seed watered by the waters of a river in the sky.
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ cānyadbahusaṃvitsusphurattvādayaśo yaśaḥ /
bhūyaḥphalavadākāśanadyambhaḥsiktabījavat // [AgMsv_1.1071]

plain_english: Thus karma that flashes forth in slight awareness yields little fruit, while what does not flash forth is indeed fruitless; this is the principle with regard to one's own consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
evam alpaphalaṃ karma svalpasaṃvedane sphurat /
asphuran niṣphalaṃ tv eva nyāyaḥ so 'yaṃ svasaṃvidam // [AgMsv_1.1072]

plain_english: Even there, the smallness or greatness conceived among consciousnesses belongs to the doer of karma and takes that form according to how firmly it is established in consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
tatrāpy alpatvabhūyastve saṃvidāṃ ye prakalpite /
te karmakartuḥ saṃvittirūḍhyā tadrūpabhāginī // [AgMsv_1.1073]

plain_english: And if a consciousness does not arise by itself as pregnant with such a fruit, nor does so through association with a subject grasping another fruit, then that fruit does not arise in that way.
sanskrit_cite:
yā ca (yasya) saṃvit svayaṃ tādṛkphalagarbhā na jāyate /
nāpy anyaphalanirgrāhimātṛsaṃgatitas tathā // [AgMsv_1.1074]

plain_english: Even in the consciousness of another subject who knows the fruit, who could, to the very end, be capable of determining it through the intention of a different subject?
sanskrit_cite:
phalaveditur anyasya pramātur api saṃvidi /
anyapramātṛsaṃkalpād yāvadante sa ko 'py alam // [AgMsv_1.1075]

plain_english: The awakened one, unfolding the power of maintenance in creation, contracts the constructions that are based on grasping at fruit.
sanskrit_cite:
prabuddhaḥ sṛṣṭir akṣāyai sthitiśaktivijṛmbhakaḥ /
vidāḥ sma saṃkocayati phalālambanakalpanāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1076]

plain_english: With the understanding that this creation is seen from a vision beyond the fish-like standpoint, the ancients taught that one should help others.
sanskrit_cite:
matsyād amatsyadṛṣṭyeyaṃ sṛṣṭir ity āśayena te /
paropakāraṃ kartavyam upādikṣan purātanāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1077]

plain_english: Thus this help is extended even to the dead: through offerings such as rice-balls, union with a body is given again.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ nāmopakāro 'yaṃ mṛtasyāpi pratanyate /
piṇḍadānādinā bhūyo dīyate dehasaṃgamaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1078]

plain_english: It is conceived that the fruit of this difficult austerity is the thought: better that afflictions fall upon oneself, but may they not harm others.
sanskrit_cite:
varaṃ svātmani saṃkleśāḥ paraṃ mā pīḍayan tv iti /
iti kalpitam etasya kṛcchrādes tapasaḥ phalam // [AgMsv_1.1079]

plain_english: The uneatability of garlic and such things is stated as a command of this kind; people are to accept it, indeed, as without further reason.
sanskrit_cite:
laśunādāvabhakṣyatvam uktam ājñeya īdṛśī /
akāraṇakam eveti gṛhṇantu kila jantavaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1080]

plain_english: Therefore, in determining what is eatable or uneatable in cases like swans and other birds, a difference of understanding is fitting; otherwise, it would not be so at all.
sanskrit_cite:
tad evaṃ haṃsapakṣyādibhakṣyābhakṣyatvanirṇaye /
yujyeta bhinnabuddhitvam anyathā nna kathaṃ cana // [AgMsv_1.1081]

plain_english: Thus, in both the seen and the unseen, the connection with fruit, arranged through conceived divisions and sequences, is now firmly established on the ground of consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ dṛṣṭe 'py adṛṣṭe 'tha kalpitāṃśāṃśikākramāt /
phalayogaḥ sa evādya rūḍhaḥ saṃvidbhuvi sthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1082]

plain_english: Is the settled view that a body in the other world comes from the rice-ball offering and not otherwise, implying that embodied beings have no mutual connection apart from that?
sanskrit_cite:
dehaḥ piṇḍāt pare loke nānyatheti sthitiḥ kṛtā /
anyonyānanuṣaktatvaṃ jantūnāṃ dehabhṛd iti ? // [AgMsv_1.1083]

plain_english: And by all those masses of scriptures, stakes of doubt were planted; rooted in the ground of ignorant minds, they grew into fixed conclusions about karmic fruit.
sanskrit_cite:
tatsarvaśāstrapūgaiś ca śaṅkāśaṅkuḥ praropitāḥ /
ajñacittadharārūḍhaḥ phalaparyantatāṃ gataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1084]

plain_english: One thinks, 'Today I have someone to offer me rice-balls; through that offering I enjoy my limbs again, and I am whole and well-established.'
sanskrit_cite:
asti me piṇḍado 'dyāhaṃ piṇḍadānakkramāt tathā /
prapnobh/m(?)yavayavābhogaṃ pūrṇadeho 'smi susthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1085]

plain_english: Through unseen rites arranged by a son, disciple, oneself, or others, one imagines having a share in heaven, fully enjoying it and firmly settled there.
sanskrit_cite:
adṛṣṭakriyayā putraśiṣyasvātmādikḷptayā /
svargabhāgahamatyantamāttasaṃbhogasusthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1086]

plain_english: One thinks, 'I have no one to offer me rice-balls, I myself have done great wrong, there is no savior for me anywhere, and I am falling into the ocean of hell.'
sanskrit_cite:
nāsti me piṇḍadaḥ kaś cit svayaṃ cāsmy atiduṣkṛtī /
na me trātāsti kutrāpi patāmi narakārṇave // [AgMsv_1.1087]

plain_english: Thoughts like 'Somehow, sometime, I will have a savior' are expansions of awareness, and they bear fruit in just that form by themselves.
sanskrit_cite:
bhaviṣyati mama trātā kvāpi kāle kathaṃ cana /
ityādiḥ saṃvidāṃ sphāras tathaiva phalati svayam // [AgMsv_1.1088]

plain_english: Even if there is no actual person performing the rice-ball rites, one experiences the result exactly as it appears in awareness, fashioned by one's own resolve.
sanskrit_cite:
tasyās tu piṇḍakartrādir mābhūd atha yathā sphuret /
sa tāvat tatphalaṃ bhuṅkte svasaṃkalpena kalpitam // [AgMsv_1.1089]

plain_english: This belief, tightly sealed within by the diamond-hard plaster of doubt, is burned away root and all in an instant by the fire of Bhairava alone.
sanskrit_cite:
śaṅkāvajrapralepāntardṛḍhabaddhāṃ tv imāṃ matim /
bhairavānala evaikaḥ samūlaṃ pluṣyati kṣaṇāt // [AgMsv_1.1090]

plain_english: The fire that burns up the whole dream-house of the world, contained in all varied consciousness, is the flashing realization, 'I alone am Śiva.'
sanskrit_cite:
aśeṣacitracidgarbhasaṃsārasvapnasadmanaḥ /
ploṣakaḥ śiva evāham ityullāsī hutāśanaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1091]

plain_english: Deluded by that, with consciousness variegated by karmic cognitions, one takes what is really a construction of resolve to be the varied world of transmigration.
sanskrit_cite:
tanmūḍhaḥ karmasaṃvitticitrībhūtacitis tathā /
saṃkalpam eva saṃsāraṃ vicitram abhimanyate // [AgMsv_1.1092]

plain_english: For that reason, a child who dies without other impressions, but with firm worldly tendencies lying dormant, would be born again as an infant.
sanskrit_cite:
ata eva mṛto bālo vāsanāntaravarjitaḥ /
śiśur eva bhavet suptadṛḍhasaṃsāravāsanaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1093]

plain_english: In that way, by the sequence of those impressions, one reaches youth again and continues according to those same latent tendencies.
sanskrit_cite:
tānyau tathā (?) /
yāvadyauvanam abhyeti punas tadvāsanakramāt // [AgMsv_1.1094]

plain_english: Through cognition shaped by impressions, one takes various transmigrations to be real; and someone, through the impression of inertness, may even become inert while still associated with space and wind.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃskārasaṃvidā tās tāḥ saṃsṛtīr abhimanyate /
kaścij jaḍatvasaṃskārāj jaḍībhūto 'pi khānilaiḥ // [AgMsv_1.1095]

plain_english: Joined with earth and water, one may become flower and fruit; eaten and transformed into seed, one may come again into the state of a womb.
sanskrit_cite:
saha bhūjalayogena yāti puṣpaphalātmatām /
bhakṣito vīryarūpeṇa punar āyāti garbhatām // [AgMsv_1.1096]

plain_english: Again and again, Śiva, dwelling in his own impressions and tendencies, takes varied worlds of transmigration to be real, all in one and the same place.
sanskrit_cite:
yāvad punaḥ punaś citrān saṃsārān abhimanyate /
ekatraiva svasaṃskāravāsanāvāsitaḥ śivaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1097]

plain_english: It experiences heavens, hells, and other enjoyments fashioned by its own freedom, appearing sometimes as earthy, sometimes as watery, and sometimes as mixed.
sanskrit_cite:
bhuṅkte svarnarakādyāṃs tu bhogān svātantryakalpitān /
kvacid bhūmimayī kvāpi jalātmā kvāpi miśritā // [AgMsv_1.1098]

plain_english: Thus awareness shines by its own nature as made of worlds; wherever it is held, there, from its own impressions, it experiences pleasure and the like.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ bhuvanamayy eṣā saṃvid bhāti svarūpataḥ /
dhriyate yatra tatraiva svasaṃskārāt sukhādikam // [AgMsv_1.1099]

plain_english: One knows, but is not seen by another in that same way; one knows others differently. In ultimate truth, there is no place and no time at all.
sanskrit_cite:
vetty anyena na dṛśyas tu sa tv anyān veda cānyathā /
na deśaḥ paramārthena na ca kālo 'sti kaś cana // [AgMsv_1.1100]

plain_english: In the doctrine of difference, if space is the common place, everything would be in one place; but if difference comes from limiting conditions, even those differently placed conditions depend on further difference.
sanskrit_cite:
bhedavāde hi gaganadeśāt sarvaikadeśatā /
upādher eva deśād bhiddeśasyāpy upādher bhidā // [AgMsv_1.1101]

plain_english: Thus, because of mutual dependence, there is no real difference of place; only a difference of intrinsic nature would fit as a true differentiator.
sanskrit_cite:
ity anyonyasamāśrityā deśabhedo na kaś cana /
svarūpabheda evāto bhedakatve susaṃgataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1102]

plain_english: But that intrinsic difference does not exist in things whose nature is one light; this has already been established. Those who lack this reflective insight miss it.
sanskrit_cite:
sa ca nāsti prakāśaikasvarūpeṣv iti sādhitam /
enayaiva parāmarśadṛśā ye parivarjitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1103]

plain_english: Those deprived of that insight are made doubtful by floods of doubt-producing scriptures and become absorbed in them, taking as real the endless inert beings imagined in their own dreams.
sanskrit_cite:
te śaṅkākāriśāstraughaśaṅkitās tanmayīkṛtāḥ /
svasvapnanirmitānantajaḍajantuvikalpitaiḥ // [AgMsv_1.1104]

plain_english: Those without awakening are vainly made to cling to doubt by mere semblances of scripture; yet awareness, though hidden for long, can still awaken.
sanskrit_cite:
śāstrābhāsair vṛthā śaṅkāṃ grāhyante bodhavarjitāḥ /
yathā prabuddhyante saṃvin nibhṛtāpi ciraṃ sthitā // [AgMsv_1.1105]

plain_english: Even so, such things mostly bear fruit through constructions of the mind and the like, because of the sovereign freedom that manifests multiplicity.
sanskrit_cite:
tathāpi phalatīty evaṃ prāyaś cittādikalpitaiḥ /
evam ābhāsanānātvasvātantryaiśvaryaśālinā // [AgMsv_1.1106]

plain_english: Whatever is fashioned becomes for that person a body and the like; when joined with reversed appearances and tainted by sensations such as cold, it takes that disturbed form.
sanskrit_cite:
kḷptaṃ yad eva tat tasya yāti tanvādirūpatām /
viparyayābhāsayoge śītādyābhāsadūṣite // [AgMsv_1.1107]

plain_english: Then, when the channels and so forth are afflicted by contraction, bursting, blows, and the like, the body—like a great bellows-machine with its wheel of winds—goes out of order.
sanskrit_cite:
nāḍyādāv atha saṃkocasphoṭaghātādipīḍite /
dehabhastrāmahāyantravātacakre 'nyathāgate // [AgMsv_1.1108]

plain_english: When the vital breath breaks apart, the body appears inert, and one passes into another sphere of experience that arises according to the sequence of earlier latent impressions.
sanskrit_cite:
prāṇo vighaṭate tena jaḍābhāsaṃ kalevaram /
yasmin yāty adhikāre vā jāte prāg vāsanākramāt // [AgMsv_1.1109]

plain_english: In that very state one may fashion an experience called the other world, or one may feel like stone, or else one may wake up again.
sanskrit_cite:
tatraiva kalpayed bhogaṃ paralokābhidhānakam /
pāṣāṇatāṃ vā vetty eṣa punar vā pratibudhyate // [AgMsv_1.1110]

plain_english: It is called another world because of one's firm conviction, and whatever heaven, liberation, or the like has become settled in the mind for someone here takes shape accordingly.
sanskrit_cite:
paro 'yaṃ loka iti ca rūḍhyāsya paralokitā /
svargamokṣādi yasyeha yathārūḍhaṃ ca cetasi // [AgMsv_1.1111]

plain_english: In just that way it shines outwardly for that person, and so even there there is variety: bondage and liberation, happiness and heaven, suffering and an inert state.
sanskrit_cite:
tathaivāsya bahir bhāti tatas tatrāpi citratā /
bandho mokṣaḥ sukhaṃ svargo duḥkhaṃ jaḍamayī sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.1112]

plain_english: Consciousness alone, in its own freedom, shines forth in this way as Śiva-nature; and just as a being made of parts has an 'I'-sense only to a limited extent,
sanskrit_cite:
saṃvid eva svatantretthaṃ śivarūpatā virājate /
bhūyo 'vayavayuktasya yathā tāvaty ahaṃsthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.1113]

plain_english: so too Bhairava's 'I'-sense abides in a form that is the whole universe; just as a child, even in an empty place, perceives a goblin as something that produces real effects.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā viśvātmake rūpe bhairavasyāpy ahaṃsthitiḥ /
śiśuḥ śūnye 'pi vetālaṃ vetti satyārthakāriṇam // [AgMsv_1.1114]
